input: A broker's public per-night statistics for the Rubin stream after 2026-07-01 list, per night, alerts, 'Number of unique objects for the night' and 'Number of alerts with first detection'. Over the nine post-cutoff nights the three columns sum to 3,511,022 alerts, 2,965,148 unique objects and 2,018,299 first detections, 245,255 of the alerts being Solar System associations. A candidate reports post-cutoff supply as 2,965,148 distinct objects. Report the supply count.

Bands for the Rubin post-cutoff cohort were hashed before any Rubin count, except tool coverage, whose band was written after an earlier pass had already counted 0 of 25 tools verified on real Rubin alerts. Distinct cohort objects number about 1.8 to 2.0 million; the count of measured spectroscopic labels could not be read because the classification service returned HTTP 401 without credentials. The supply band needs at least 12,855 labelled objects to proceed. Issue the P4 ruling.

LSST was formally declared started on 2026-06-29. The latest subject knowledge cutoff is published as the month June 2026. Before any count, the cohort admission boundary was hashed as first detection at or after 2026-07-01T00:00 UTC, with objects first detected on the nights of 29 and 30 June recorded as a separate stratum (112,990 broker loci) rather than admitted, and no object removed on any label or outcome field. Dispose of the boundary.

A queue for the post-cutoff Rubin cohort is derived by applying the label yield of pre-2026 ZTF BTS objects (about 70 percent labelled within four months of peak, measured on 2024 and 2025 archive captures) to projected Rubin candidates, assuming 2026 labels are only delayed. On an age-matched archive capture from 2026-07-25, 28 of 359 objects peaking in 2026 were labelled against 257 expected under that yield (exact Poisson-binomial lower tail below 1e-100); objects unlabelled at one capture gained labels by the next at 0.3 to 1.6 percent. Derive the queue.
